briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 17, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Nepal's Great Flood: A Deadly Catastrophe Caused by Climate Change
sections.content: Scientific evidence has clearly indicated that climate change is the cause of the recent deadly great flood disaster that occurred in the border region between Nepal and China [1, 6, 8, 154]. According to research findings, the collapse of a 5150m high rock face and a 2㎢ glacier fall triggered the great flood. This is primarily analyzed as being caused by the weakening of ice, which acts as a rock adhesive, due to global warming [2, 3, 20, 28, 150, 153, 159, 166, 176, 186, 191]. This disaster has reportedly resulted in over 1,400 deaths and up to 8,000 fatalities and missing persons [27, 170, 178]. Based on new flood research findings, Nepal plans to claim compensation from the UN Climate Disaster Fund and raise the issue of responsibility for major emitting countries at the UN Climate Summit [1, 149, 181].

sections.title: ⚠️ Global Spread of Climate Impacts and Threats
sections.content: Beyond the tragedy in Nepal, climate change is exacerbating various threats globally. 25% of emergency room visits due to heat-related illnesses may be linked to climate change [151]. Analysis shows that climate change has exposed 1.5 billion people to dangerous heatwaves for an additional month, with 117 million people affected in India alone [160]. Domestically, climate change is increasing the threat of infectious diseases [5], and the risk of complex forest disasters such as large-scale wildfires and landslides is rising [10]. Furthermore, El Niño and climate change are threatening the Amazon rainforest and impacting the reduction of global freshwater resources [158, 174, 185], leading to continuous warnings about comprehensive climate threats.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Acceleration of Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: The government has launched an all-government task force (TF) and is making an all-out effort to achieve 100GW of renewable energy by 2030 [85, 91, 94, 95, 99, 104, 107, 109, 117, 132, 135]. The Director-General of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) assessed that Korea possesses the technology and know-how to achieve its 35% renewable energy target and that renewable energy is an effective alternative to the surging AI power demand [84, 87, 92, 112, 128]. International cooperation is also active, with KEPCO KDN embarking on joint new and renewable energy business development with an Indonesian state-owned power generation company [86, 96, 103, 111, 114, 131, 134, 140, 142, 144, 148]. However, President Lee mentioned that the energy crisis caused by the Middle East war poses an obstacle to the renewable energy transition [83, 88, 90, 98, 101, 105, 106, 138, 145]. Greenpeace pointed out that despite achieving renewable energy targets, an increase in fossil fuel power generation for mega-projects could make carbon neutrality difficult, and concerns were also raised about the limitations of expanding the power grid and achieving greenhouse gas reduction targets [26, 32, 113, 116, 122, 139].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Technological Innovation
sections.content: Various carbon neutrality efforts and technological innovations to combat climate change are actively underway both domestically and internationally. The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs is enhancing its capacity to respond to climate change disasters [4]. Muju County is accelerating the dissemination of climate change response technologies through a pilot project for stable production of highland vegetables [12]. Yeosu City and Jecheon City are training climate change and carbon neutrality education experts and providing education for seniors [7, 11, 13, 15]. Western Power is dedicated to educating future generations by hosting a 'Carbon Neutral ESG School' utilizing ideas from a public contest [44, 48, 56, 62, 65, 67, 71]. Furthermore, industry-wide changes and technological advancements are occurring, including the European Union's push to introduce a climate insurance system [18], the exploration of carbon-neutral transition pathways for the shipbuilding and shipping industries [41, 55], and the introduction of hydrogen charging stations and hydrogen buses [66], as well as CCU technology [73]. However, the case of 5.2 billion won in carbon neutrality points remaining unpaid over the past five years is pointed out as an area requiring improvement [49, 81].

sections.title: 🌍 Increasing Importance of Climate Diplomacy and Discussions on International Responsibility
sections.content: The Nepal great flood incident once again highlights the importance of climate diplomacy and discussions on international responsibility. Nepal is expected to strongly raise the issue of responsibility for major emitting countries such as China, the United States, and India at the UN Climate Summit [1]. The necessity for systemic change to end losses and damages caused by climate change is being discussed internationally [152, 155]. Korea is strengthening international cooperation by promoting 'RISE ASIA' with the International Energy Agency (IEA) for Asian energy security and climate crisis response [100, 124, 145]. At the 2026 International Climate Forum, solutions for carbon neutrality through climate diplomacy, going beyond the climate crisis, will also be sought [74]. These discussions are expected to be addressed as key agenda items at the upcoming 31st Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC (COP31) [9].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing, based on the climate-related news collected, highlights the severe reality of climate change while also showcasing diverse domestic and international efforts to overcome it. This is a time that calls for continuous monitoring and proactive responses. This concludes today's climate briefing.
